name: tpm_crb_ffa_to_linux_errno
prose: Precondition: none; errno may be any int. Postcondition: a pure switch over errno with no side effects; it returns 0 for 0x05000001 (CRB_FFA_OK) or 0x05000002 (CRB_FFA_OK_RESULTS_RETURNED), -ENOENT for 0x8e000001, -EPERM for 0x8e000002, -EINVAL for 0x8e000005, -ENOEXEC for 0x8e000006, -EEXIST for 0x8e000009, -EACCES for 0x8e00000a, -ENOMEM for 0x8e00000b, and -EINVAL (default case) for every other value.
note: checked lines 128-165 of tpm_crb_ffa.c: single switch, one return rc, default is -EINVAL. Contract left empty because the return values are errno names.

name: init_nsc
prose: Precondition: init_nsc is the __init module entry point, called once at load with no arguments; it probes the Super-I/O ports itself. Behaviour: it reads the SID index at TPM_ADDR; if that is not 0xEF it computes a base address from Super-I/O registers 0x2C/0x2B and reads the SID there, returning -ENODEV (nothing acquired) if that is not 0xF6. It then calls platform_driver_register(&nsc_drv) and returns its error code if nonzero, reads the base from the NSC BASE0 registers, writes 0x01 to the NSC_LDC_INDEX register, and allocates the platform device "tpm_nscl0" (-ENOMEM, driver unregistered, if that fails; the global pdev is assigned either way). It sets pdev->dev.release to tpm_nsc_remove, calls platform_device_add (its negative return is propagated), devm_kzalloc for priv (-ENOMEM), request_region(base, 2) (-EBUSY if it fails) and tpmm_chip_alloc (-ENODEV if it returns an error pointer), then sets priv as the chip device's drvdata and calls tpm_chip_register, whose nonzero return is propagated. On success it logs debug and info messages and returns 0, leaving the driver registered, the device added, the 2-byte I/O region requested and the chip registered. On every failure after the driver was registered it jumps through err_rel_reg (release_region), err_del_dev (platform_device_del), err_put_dev (platform_device_put) and err_unreg_drv (platform_driver_unregister) from the failing point onward and returns rc. platform_device_put drops the last reference to pdev and so runs the release callback tpm_nsc_remove, which reads dev_get_drvdata of the platform device and dereferences it as a chip; this function never sets that drvdata, so those error paths do not return cleanly the way a plain unwind would.
note: checked tpm_nsc.c 289-399. Reviewer round 15 claim is RIGHT (put -> tpm_nsc_remove with unset drvdata, lines 325,394-395,257-266); round 1 claim (omits tpmm_chip_alloc -ENODEV) is also right at line 343-346; the order in the old prose (device_add after kzalloc) was also wrong: device_add is line 327, devm_kzalloc 330.

name: xillybus_write
prose: Precondition: filp->private_data is the xilly_channel for the open file, userbuf is a user pointer for count bytes, and the caller does not hold channel->rd_mutex. Behaviour: returns -EIO immediately if endpoint->fatal_error is set; otherwise it takes rd_mutex with mutex_lock_interruptible and returns that error if interrupted. In a loop it reserves space in the current host DMA buffer under rd_spinlock, copies from userbuf with copy_from_user, and when a buffer is completed it syncs it for the device and submits it to the FPGA by iowrite32 under register_mutex. If copy_from_user fails (rc = -EFAULT) the code finishes any submission for that buffer, unlocks rd_mutex, and returns -EIO if fatal_error is set, otherwise queues the rd_workitem if the channel is not rd_synchronous and returns -EFAULT. The loop stops when bytes_done >= count, or when the buffers are exhausted and bytes_done > 0 and rd_allow_partial is set, or when the buffers are exhausted and O_NONBLOCK is set (rc = -EAGAIN, even if bytes_done is nonzero); otherwise it waits interruptibly on rd_wait with the mutex held, and if that wait is interrupted it unlocks rd_mutex and returns -EIO if fatal_error, else bytes_done if nonzero, else -EINTR, without queueing the workitem. After a normal loop exit it unlocks rd_mutex, queues rd_workitem if the channel is not rd_synchronous, returns -EIO if fatal_error, returns rc (-EAGAIN) if set, and if the channel is rd_synchronous and bytes_done > 0 calls xillybus_myflush and returns its result unless it is 0 or -EINTR; finally it returns bytes_done. rd_mutex is not held on any return.
note: checked xillybus_core.c 1201-1424 (slice cut the head). Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT: the copy-failure path (1354-1366) returns -EIO on fatal_error without queueing; the old prose omitted that and also the -EAGAIN-discards-byte-count behaviour.

name: xillybus_read
prose: Precondition: filp->private_data is the xilly_channel, userbuf is a user pointer writable for count bytes, and the caller does not hold channel->wr_mutex. Behaviour: returns -EIO immediately if endpoint->fatal_error is set; otherwise takes wr_mutex interruptibly and returns that error on failure. It then loops, copying data from the current host DMA buffer to userbuf with copy_to_user under wr_spinlock bookkeeping, handing completed buffers back to the FPGA with iowrite32, and sometimes dropping and re-taking wr_mutex while it waits on wr_wait. If copy_to_user fails it unlocks wr_mutex and returns -EFAULT immediately (without checking fatal_error). The loop ends when bytes_done >= count (a count of zero ends here with 0), when EOF is reached (wr_empty and host buffer index equal to wr_eof, which also ends the loop with the bytes copied so far, possibly 0), when data has been copied and the read is nonblocking, when bytes_done > 0 and either the timeout budget ran out or the channel is synchronous with partial reads allowed, or when O_NONBLOCK is set, no time budget flag is set, nothing was copied and the FPGA has no data ready (rc = -EAGAIN). If a nonblocking read has nothing copied but the FPGA reports ready data, it jumps to the label that sets the no-time-left flag and writes a flush-all request to the FPGA, and then loops again. After a normal exit it unlocks wr_mutex and returns -EIO if fatal_error, rc if nonzero, otherwise bytes_done. If a wait is interrupted it returns without holding wr_mutex: -EIO if fatal_error, else bytes_done if nonzero, else -EAGAIN if O_NONBLOCK (only on the path through the label interrupted), else -EINTR.
note: checked xillybus_core.c 690-1005 (slice cut head). Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT: no-data returns -EAGAIN for nonblocking (line 841) or blocks, 0 is returned only for count==0 or EOF; old prose wrong on that and omitted -EAGAIN on interrupted nonblocking waits (line 936).

name: xillyusb_open
prose: Precondition: called as the open handler with the inode of a xillyusb channel and a file whose f_mode/f_flags give the requested access. Behaviour: under kref_mutex it calls xillybus_find_inode and returns its error directly if nonzero (no reference taken); otherwise it takes a kref on the device, stores the channel in filp->private_data and locks chan->lock. It fails with -ENODEV (dropping the kref and chan->lock, open flags untouched) if xdev->error is set, if the channel is not readable/writable as requested, or if O_NONBLOCK is requested with a synchronous read or write stream; it fails with -EBUSY the same way if the channel is already open in a requested direction. Otherwise it sets open_for_read and/or open_for_write and unlocks. For write it allocates an endpoint (-ENOMEM on failure), fifo_init on its FIFO, sets fill_mask, out_bytes and flushed and calls flush_downstream with a timeout, turning -ETIMEDOUT into -EIO (reported with report_io_error); any such failure jumps to late_unopen. For read it kzallocs and fifo_init's an in_fifo (-ENOMEM or the fifo_init error, freeing in_fifo, then late_unopen). It then publishes in_fifo (read_data_ok = 1) and out_ep under chan->lock, and for read sends OPCODE_SET_CHECKPOINT via xillyusb_send_opcode; if that fails it goes to unfifo (read_data_ok cleared, in_fifo unassigned and freed, out_ep cleared) then falls into late_unopen. On success it returns 0 (calls request_read_anything for O_NONBLOCK reads, ignoring errors) with the kref retained. late_unopen deallocates out_ep if one exists, and unopen clears the open flags for the requested directions under chan->lock and puts the kref, returning the error.
note: checked xillyusb.c 1236-1429. Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT: -EBUSY/-ENODEV paths (goto unmutex_fail at 1264-1288) do not clear the open flags; old prose claimed they were cleared on every error.

name: sam9x60_clk_register_div_pll
prose: Precondition: regmap, lock, layout and characteristics are valid pointers (layout is dereferenced for layout->div2), and name/parent are valid for clk_hw_register. Behaviour: it returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) if id > PLL_MAX_ID, lock is NULL, or safe_div is nonzero while the global notifier_div is already set; it clamps safe_div to PLL_DIV_MAX - 1 if it is PLL_DIV_MAX or more; it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if kzalloc fails. It chooses the clk ops (fixed-div ops if layout->div2, else the gated or the change-rate ops depending on CLK_SET_RATE_GATE in flags), fills the sam9x60_div, and under the lock with interrupts saved writes the PLL id to AT91_PMC_PLL_UPDT and reads the current divider from AT91_PMC_PLL_CTRL0 into div->div (regmap return values are ignored). It then calls clk_hw_register(NULL, hw); on error it frees div and returns ERR_PTR(ret); on success, if div->safe_div is nonzero it stores div in the global notifier_div and calls clk_notifier_register (return value ignored); it returns the clk_hw.
note: slice cut the head: real function is sam9x60_clk_register_div_pll (clk-sam9x60-pll.c:725-796); old name 'sam9x60_div_pll_register' does not exist; old prose missed the three early error returns.

name: iproc_armpll_setup
prose: Precondition: node is a device-tree node for an iProc ARM PLL (an __init function called once at setup). Behaviour: it returns void. It kzallocs a struct iproc_arm_pll (WARN_ON and return if that fails), maps register block 0 with of_iomap (WARN_ON; kfree the pll and return if that fails), fills a clk_init_data using node->name, iproc_arm_pll_ops (recalc_rate only), flags 0 and the first parent name from of_clk_get_parent_name if one exists (one parent) else none, and calls clk_hw_register(NULL, &pll->hw). If registration fails it warns, unmaps the registers and frees the pll. It then calls of_clk_add_hw_provider with of_clk_hw_simple_get; if that fails it warns, calls clk_hw_unregister, unmaps the registers and frees the pll. On success it returns with the clock and provider registered and pll and its mapping retained. No error is returned to the caller.
note: slice 257-273 is the tail of iproc_armpll_setup (clk-iproc-armpll.c:232-273: the function head is missing); fixed under the real name instead of dropping. Old prose 'all previously completed steps are undone' is right for the three goto labels.

name: iproc_asiu_setup
prose: Precondition: node is a device-tree node, div and gate point to arrays of at least num_clks entries, and the function is an __init routine called once. Behaviour: it returns void. It returns immediately if gate or div is NULL (WARN_ON). It kzallocs the iproc_asiu, its clk_data (struct_size with num_clks hws) and its clks array (kcalloc), maps register blocks 0 (div_base) and 1 (gate_base) with of_iomap, then for each clock i reads clock-output-names[i], fills in the clock and registers it with clk_hw_register, storing the hw in clk_data->hws[i]; finally it calls of_clk_add_hw_provider with of_clk_hw_onecell_get. Any failure after allocations (WARN_ON in each case) jumps to the unwind labels: err_clk_register unregisters the clocks registered so far (hws[i-1] down to hws[0]) and unmaps gate_base, then err_iomap_gate unmaps div_base, err_iomap_div frees clks, err_asiu_clks frees clk_data and err_clks frees the asiu; a failure at an earlier allocation or mapping enters the chain at the matching later label, so only what was already acquired is released. On success nothing is freed and the asiu, mappings and registered clocks remain.
note: slice 255-266 is only the err_* unwind tail of iproc_asiu_setup (clk-iproc-asiu.c:175-266), which is a real function; label is not a function so fixed under real name. Verified labels: err_clk_register -> err_iomap_gate -> err_iomap_div -> err_asiu_clks -> err_clks (lines 247-266).

name: iproc_pll_clk_setup
prose: Precondition: node is a device-tree node for an iProc PLL, pll_ctrl and clk_ctrl point to valid descriptors, num_clks is at least 1 (hws[0] is written unconditionally), and the function is called once at setup. Behaviour: it returns void. It returns immediately if pll_ctrl or clk_ctrl is NULL (WARN_ON). It then itself allocates pll, clk_data (num_clks hw pointers) and an iclk array, maps control_base from register block 0 (failure is fatal), maps pwr_base from block 1 (failure tolerated), maps asiu_base from block 2 if IPROC_CLK_PLL_ASIU is set (failure is fatal), and maps status_base from block 2 if IPROC_CLK_PLL_SPLIT_STAT_CTRL is set (failure is fatal), otherwise status_base aliases control_base. It reads clock-output-names[0], stores vco/num_vco_entries when vco is non-NULL, applies the software-override setting via iproc_pll_sw_cfg, registers the PLL clock with clk_hw_register and then registers clocks 1 to num_clks-1 each after reading clock-output-names[i], and adds an of_clk_hw_onecell_get provider. On a failure in the clock-name read, a registration, or the provider add, it unregisters the clocks registered so far (for failures in the leaf loop or the provider add), unmaps status_base only when it differs from control_base, unmaps asiu_base and pwr_base when non-NULL, unmaps control_base, and frees iclk_array, clk_data and pll; a failure earlier in the mapping chain enters this unwind at a later label so the status_base mapping is not unmapped when the status_base mapping itself failed. On success it keeps the allocations and mappings.
note: slice cut the head; real function is iproc_pll_clk_setup (clk-iproc-pll.c:712-863), no function iproc_pll_clk_probe exists in this file. Old prose wrongly says the caller allocated pll/clk_data/iclk_array and mapped control_base: the function allocates and maps them itself (lines 731-755).

name: kona_dt_ccu_setup
prose: Precondition: ccu points to a ccu_data whose kona_clks array and clk_num are populated and node is a device-tree node. Behaviour: it returns void. It reads register resource 0 of node with of_address_to_resource, rejects (goto out_err) a failure or a resource size above U32_MAX, stores the size in ccu->range, rejects the setup if ccu_data_valid(ccu) is false, ioremaps the block into ccu->base (out_err if NULL), takes a node reference with of_node_get into ccu->node, calls kona_clk_setup for each kona_clks entry whose ccu field is non-NULL, and calls of_clk_add_hw_provider with of_clk_kona_onecell_get (out_err if it fails). If kona_ccu_init(ccu) returns false it only prints an error and the setup stays in place. On the out_err path it calls kona_ccu_teardown and prints a message; kona_ccu_teardown returns doing nothing if ccu->base is still NULL, and otherwise deletes the provider, tears down the clocks, puts the node reference, clears ccu->node and unmaps and clears ccu->base. ccu->range is left set when a failure occurs after it was stored.
note: slice cut the head; real function is kona_dt_ccu_setup (clk-kona-setup.c:790-855), no kona_ccu_setup. Old prose matches the code except it implied teardown always releases something and omitted that ccu->range remains set.

name: imx_clk_hw_pllv2
prose: Precondition: name and parent are valid strings and base is a mapped register base. Behaviour: it kzallocs a struct clk_pllv2 and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if that fails. Otherwise it stores base, fills a clk_init_data (name, clk_pllv2_ops, flags 0, one parent name taken from the parent argument) and calls clk_hw_register(NULL, &pll->hw). If registration fails it frees the clk_pllv2 and returns ERR_PTR(ret) with that error; on success it returns &pll->hw, with the allocation kept for the registered clock.
note: slice cut the head; real name is imx_clk_hw_pllv2 (clk-pllv2.c:249-279). Removed the old claim that the clock core keeps the name/parent pointers without copying, since nothing in this function shows that.

name: module_platform_driver(clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv)
prose: Generated function clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv_init, expanded from module_platform_driver(clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv) via module_driver: it is an __init function that takes no arguments and returns the value of platform_driver_register(&clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv); it is registered with module_init. It does nothing else.
note: names in the packet (clk_mt6765_mipi0a_init) do not exist; module_driver (include/linux/device/driver.h:257-267) names the functions <driver>_init and <driver>_exit.

name: module_platform_driver(clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv)
prose: Generated function clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv_exit, expanded from module_platform_driver(clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv) via module_driver: it is an __exit function that takes no arguments, calls platform_driver_unregister(&clk_mt6765_mipi0a_drv), returns nothing, and does nothing else; it is registered with module_exit.
note: same macro expansion as item 0; module_driver in include/linux/device/driver.h:263-266.

name: rate_from_params
prose: Precondition: n2 is the integer divider and sdm the fractional numerator; parent_rate is an unsigned long. Behaviour: a pure computation. It computes divisor = SDM_DEN * n2 + sdm (SDM_DEN is 16384) in unsigned long before checking anything; if n2 < N2_MIN (4) it returns -EINVAL. Otherwise it returns DIV_ROUND_UP_ULL((u64)parent_rate * SDM_DEN, divisor), i.e. the quotient of parent_rate * 16384 over the divisor rounded up, converted to long. It touches no lock, memory or global state; the multiplication, divisor computation and the narrowing to long are not guarded against overflow.
note: clk-mpll.c:31-41. Contract left empty because the function returns -EINVAL and the contract cannot express the overflow cases.

name: PARM_SET
note: macro in parm.h:17-18 expands to an expression ((reg & CLRPMASK) | (val << shift)); it is not a function, so dropped.

name: mvebu_clk_gating_setup
prose: Precondition: np is a device-tree node and desc points to an array of clk_gating_soc_desc entries terminated by an entry with a NULL name; ctrl_gating_lock has already been initialised. Behaviour: it returns void. If the file-level global ctrl is already non-NULL it prints an error and returns with nothing changed. It maps register block 0 with of_iomap (WARN_ON and return if that fails), reads the first clock with of_clk_get and, if that succeeds, takes its name as the default parent and then calls clk_put. It kzallocs the global ctrl (on failure: WARN_ON, unmaps the register base and returns), counts the descriptors, kcalloc's ctrl->gates (on failure: WARN_ON, frees ctrl, unmaps base and returns; the global pointer ctrl is not reset to NULL), then registers one clock gate per descriptor with clk_register_gate using the descriptor's parent or the default parent; a failed registration is only warned about and the ERR_PTR is stored in ctrl->gates[n]. It then calls of_clk_add_provider and register_syscore, ignoring their return values, and returns with ctrl, the gates array and the mapping retained.
note: slice cut the head; real function is mvebu_clk_gating_setup (mvebu/common.c:238-298). Old prose omitted the early return when ctrl already exists and the dangling global ctrl after the gates_out path (lines 290-295).

name: mxs_saif_clkmux_select
prose: Precondition: clkmux is any unsigned int. Behaviour: if clkmux > 3 it returns -EINVAL with no register access. Otherwise it performs two relaxed writes to the DIGCTRL register block (a write of 0x3 << BP_SAIF_CLKMUX to the CLR alias and then clkmux << BP_SAIF_CLKMUX to the SET alias) and returns 0. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: clk-imx28.c:68-77. Contract dropped because the function writes hardware registers (global state) and returns an errno.

name: spear1340_clk_init
prose: Precondition: misc_base is the mapped SPEAr1340 miscellaneous-register base (the register-offset macros such as SPEAR1340_PLL_CFG expand to misc_base + offset), the file-level spinlock _lock and the rate/parent tables are defined, and the function is an __init routine called once. Behaviour: it returns void. In a long straight-line sequence it registers the SPEAr1340 clock tree with the common clock framework: fixed-rate oscillator and pad clocks, three mux-plus-VCO/PLL pairs and a fourth VCO/PLL fed by osc_24m_clk, two fixed-rate PLL outputs, fixed-factor clocks, fractional synthesizers, aux (synthesizer plus gate) clocks, muxes and peripheral gate clocks, calling clk_register_clkdev for each result it names. It contains no conditional branches, returns nothing and does not check any return value: a clk_register_* result, possibly an ERR_PTR, is passed to clk_register_clkdev directly, and the thermal_clk fixed-factor result is not given a clkdev entry.
note: slice cut the head; real function is spear1340_clk_init (spear1340_clock.c:439-1012, body has no if/goto/return; checked lines 443-1011). Old claim 'caller acquires no new references' dropped (not visible in code).

name: spear3xx_clk_init
prose: Precondition: called once as an __init routine with misc_base the mapped SPEAr3xx miscellaneous-register base (the register macros such as PLL1_CTR and PERIP1_CLK_ENB expand to misc_base + offset, so misc_base is used), soc_config_base the SoC-config register base (only used by the SPEAr320 initializer), and the file-level _lock defined. Behaviour: it returns void. In a straight-line sequence it registers the common SPEAr3xx clocks with the common clock framework (fixed-rate oscillators and pll3_clk, the rtc and watchdog clocks, VCO/PLL pairs, fixed-factor, divider, mux, aux synthesizer and gate clocks including the ras_* gates), calling clk_register_clkdev for each result and ignoring all return values; ras_apb_clk is one of the clocks it registers. At the end it calls spear300_clk_init() if of_machine_is_compatible("st,spear300"), else spear310_clk_init() if "st,spear310", else spear320_clk_init(soc_config_base, ras_apb_clk) if "st,spear320"; if none matches it calls none of them (those three are empty inline stubs when their SoC config option is off).
note: slice cut head; function in spear3xx_clock.c:388-665. Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT: misc_base is used through the PLL1_CTR/PERIP1_CLK_ENB etc. macros (spear3xx_clock.c:20-95), old prose said it was never used. Dropped the exhaustive clock list; the full list was not re-verified line by line.

name: tegra_clk_register_sdmmc_mux_div
prose: Precondition: name, clk_base, offset, clk_num, div_flags, flags and lock describe the SDMMC clock; clk_num selects a peripheral register bank. Behaviour: it fills a stack clk_init_data (tegra_clk_sdmmc_mux_ops, the mux_sdmmc_parents array) and then looks up the register bank with get_reg_bank(clk_num); if that returns NULL it returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL). It kzallocs a tegra_sdmmc_mux and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if that fails. It fills in the register address (clk_base + offset), lock, gate fields (clk_base, bank, enable refcount periph_clk_enb_refcnt, clk_num, TEGRA_PERIPH_ON_APB), div_flags and gate_ops, and calls clk_register(NULL, ...). If clk_register returns an error pointer it frees the sdmmc_mux and returns that error pointer; otherwise it stores the returned clk in the gate's hw.clk and returns it.
note: slice cut head; real name tegra_clk_register_sdmmc_mux_div (clk-sdmmc-mux.c:234-278). Old prose omitted the get_reg_bank -EINVAL early return (lines 249-251).

name: tegra20_clk_register_emc
prose: Precondition: ioaddr is the mapped EMC register base and low_jitter the low-jitter flag. Behaviour: it kzallocs a tegra_clk_emc and returns NULL (not an error pointer) if that fails. Otherwise it fills a clk_init_data named "emc" with tegra_clk_emc_ops, flags CLK_IS_CRITICAL and the emc_parent_clk_names parents, sets reg to ioaddr and want_low_jitter to low_jitter, and calls clk_register(NULL, &emc->hw). If that returns an error pointer it frees the tegra_clk_emc and returns NULL; otherwise it returns the registered clk.
note: slice cut head; real name tegra20_clk_register_emc (clk-tegra20-emc.c:246-280). Removed the 'caller owns' wording.

name: tegra210_plle_hw_sequence_start
prose: Precondition: the file-level clk_base is a valid mapping of the clock-and-reset registers; the function takes no lock itself. Behaviour: if tegra210_plle_hw_sequence_is_enabled() is true (PLLE_AUX_SEQ_ENABLE already set) it returns 0 without writing anything. Otherwise it reads PLLE_MISC0 and returns -EIO, without any register write, if PLLE_MISC_LOCK is clear. Otherwise it clears PLLE_MISC_IDDQ_SW_CTRL in PLLE_MISC0 and writes it back, reads PLLE_AUX, sets PLLE_AUX_USE_LOCKDET and PLLE_AUX_SS_SEQ_INCLUDE and clears PLLE_AUX_ENABLE_SWCTL and PLLE_AUX_SS_SWCTL, writes it, delays 1 microsecond via fence_udelay, sets PLLE_AUX_SEQ_ENABLE, writes it again, delays again and returns 0.
note: clk-tegra210.c:512-540 and :500-509. Contract left empty because the function does register I/O and returns -EIO; reviewer's earlier point about the early return 0 was right.

name: ttc_rate_change_clocksource_cb
prose: Precondition: nb is the notifier block embedded in the ttc_timer of a ttc_timer_clocksource, data points to a clk_notifier_data, and for PRE_RATE_CHANGE both old_rate and new_rate are nonzero (they are divisors). Behaviour: PRE_RATE_CHANGE: it computes factor as the rounded ratio of the larger to the smaller rate and returns NOTIFY_BAD if factor is not a power of two or if |rate_high - factor * rate_low| exceeds MAX_F_ERR; otherwise it reads TTC_CLK_CNTRL into scale_clk_ctrl_reg_old, computes the new prescaler value by subtracting (new_rate < old_rate) or adding log2(factor) and returns NOTIFY_BAD, with the old value already saved but nothing written to hardware, if that value does not fit the prescaler field; otherwise it stores the new register value in scale_clk_ctrl_reg_new and returns NOTIFY_DONE without writing when new_rate < old_rate, or writes the new value to TTC_CLK_CNTRL and returns NOTIFY_DONE when new_rate >= old_rate. POST_RATE_CHANGE: returns NOTIFY_OK without a write when new_rate > old_rate, otherwise writes scale_clk_ctrl_reg_new to TTC_CLK_CNTRL and returns NOTIFY_DONE. ABORT_RATE_CHANGE: returns NOTIFY_OK without a write when new_rate < old_rate, otherwise writes scale_clk_ctrl_reg_old and returns NOTIFY_DONE. Any other event returns NOTIFY_DONE without a write. It takes no lock and the only state it modifies is the two saved register values and the TTC_CLK_CNTRL register.
note: slice cut head; function at timer-cadence-ttc.c:237-329. Reviewer round 15 claim (extra NOTIFY_BAD when the clocksource is enabled) is WRONG for this tree: no cs.enabled test exists anywhere in lines 237-329.

name: msm_local_timer_dying_cpu
prose: Precondition: cpu is a CPU index and msm_evt is the per-CPU clock_event_device array; the function is the dying-CPU hotplug callback installed with cpuhp_setup_state in msm_timer_init whether or not the timer uses a per-CPU interrupt. Behaviour: it takes that CPU's evt (per_cpu_ptr(msm_evt, cpu)), calls disable_percpu_irq(evt->irq), and returns 0 on its only return path. disable_percpu_irq acts on the calling CPU (smp_processor_id) and only does something if evt->irq is a per-CPU-devid interrupt (the PPI case, where it was enabled with enable_percpu_irq); if the interrupt was instead requested with request_irq (the non-PPI case in msm_local_timer_starting_cpu), the descriptor lookup fails and the call has no effect, so that interrupt is not disabled here.
note: timer-qcom.c:129-135, 98-127, 155-180; kernel/irq/irqdesc.c:859-865 (__irq_get_desc_lock returns NULL for non-percpu-devid irq under IRQ_GET_DESC_CHECK_PERCPU). Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT; round 2 claim (precondition false for non-PPI) RIGHT.

name: parse_insn
prose: Precondition: dev->mutex is held, and insn and data are the instruction and its data buffer (data must have insn->n valid entries; INSN_GTOD, INSN_WAIT, INSN_INTTRIG and INSN_DEVICE_CONFIG read or write data[0..]); file identifies the caller for the subdevice lock check. Behaviour: for an instruction with INSN_MASK_SPECIAL set, INSN_GTOD returns -EINVAL unless insn->n == 2, otherwise it stores the current seconds and microseconds in data[0] and data[1] and returns 2; INSN_WAIT returns -EINVAL unless insn->n == 1 and data[0] < 100000, otherwise it delays data[0]/1000 microseconds and returns 1; INSN_INTTRIG returns -EINVAL if insn->n != 1, if insn->subdev is out of range or if the subdevice has no async, -EAGAIN if async->inttrig is NULL, and otherwise returns the inttrig callback's negative result as is or 1 if it returned a non-negative value; INSN_DEVICE_CONFIG returns -EINVAL if check_insn_device_config_length rejects the instruction, returns 0 for INSN_DEVICE_CONFIG_GET_ROUTES after setting data[1] to the pair capacity and letting get_valid_routes overwrite data[1] with the driver's count, and otherwise returns dev->insn_device_config's result; any other special instruction returns -EINVAL. For a subdevice instruction it returns, without modifying s->busy, -EINVAL for an out-of-range subdevice or a bad chanspec, -EIO for an unused subdevice, -EACCES if the subdevice is locked by another file and -EBUSY if s->busy is already set. Otherwise it sets s->busy to parse_insn, runs INSN_READ (insn_read result), INSN_WRITE (-EINVAL if any data value exceeds the channel's maxdata, else the insn_write result), INSN_BITS (-EINVAL unless insn->n == 2, else the insn_bits result, with the mask and data shifted by the chanspec channel when n_chan <= 32 and restored afterwards), INSN_CONFIG (-EINVAL if check_insn_config_length rejects it, else the insn_config result) or any other insn value (-EINVAL), then sets s->busy back to NULL on all of those paths and returns the result, which may be a negative errno or the callback's non-negative value. Data may be modified by the instruction.
note: checked comedi_fops.c:1326-1524 and get_valid_routes (always returns 0). All three reviewer claims RIGHT: GET_ROUTES returns 0 (1395-1402), s->busy is set only at line 1451 after the early checks, and INSN_INTTRIG returns -EINVAL when there is no async (1376-1380).

name: do_cmd_ioctl
prose: Precondition: dev->mutex is held, cmd is a user-supplied comedi_cmd copy, copy points to a bool, and file identifies the caller. Behaviour: it first calls __comedi_get_user_cmd and returns its error (-ENODEV, -EIO or -EINVAL) if nonzero. It then saves the user chanlist pointer and returns -EACCES if the subdevice is locked by another file, -EBUSY if s->busy is set, or -EINVAL if cmd->chanlist_len < 1; none of these three changes the subdevice. It copies *cmd into async->cmd (with data NULL) and loads the chanlist with __comedi_get_user_chanlist (on failure it goes to cleanup with that error), calls the driver's do_cmdtest, and if the result is nonzero or CMDF_BOGUS is set copies the tested command back to *cmd, restores cmd->chanlist to the user pointer, sets cmd->data to NULL, sets *copy to true and goes to cleanup with -EAGAIN. If async->prealloc_bufsz is 0 it goes to cleanup with -ENOMEM. Otherwise it resets the buffer, sets cb_mask, updates the subdevice run flags to running, sets s->busy to file and calls the driver's do_cmd; if do_cmd returns 0 it returns 0 leaving the subdevice busy and running, otherwise it falls into cleanup. The cleanup label calls do_become_nonbusy (clears the running flag, resets the buffer, clears inttrig, frees the kernel chanlist copy, clears s->busy, wakes waiters) and returns the error.
note: slice cut head; function is comedi_fops.c:1790-1879. Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT on both counts: the function calls __comedi_get_user_cmd itself (1801) and the successful path returns 0 at 1872-1873 without do_become_nonbusy.

name: do_cmdtest_ioctl
prose: Precondition: dev->mutex is held, cmd is a user-supplied comedi_cmd copy, and copy points to a bool. Behaviour: it first calls __comedi_get_user_cmd and returns its error if nonzero, leaving *copy unchanged. It saves the user chanlist pointer; if that pointer is non-NULL it loads the chanlist with __comedi_get_user_chanlist, and on failure returns that error with cmd->chanlist set to NULL by the helper, *copy unchanged and no kernel copy left allocated. It then calls the subdevice's do_cmdtest(dev, s, cmd), frees cmd->chanlist (kfree, harmless on NULL), restores cmd->chanlist to the saved user pointer, sets *copy to true and returns the do_cmdtest result unchanged (cmd may have been modified by the driver). The subdevice is not made busy and no lock is taken.
note: slice cut head; function is comedi_fops.c:1895-1931. All three reviewer claims RIGHT: it calls __comedi_get_user_cmd itself (1905), the chanlist-load failure returns early (1917-1919) with chanlist NULL (1758).

name: apci1500_timer_insn_config
prose: Precondition: s is the counter subdevice, data holds insn->n entries (data[1] and data[2] are accessed by the operations that use them), and chan is CR_CHAN(insn->chanspec). Behaviour: it switches on data[0]. INSN_CONFIG_ARM writes data[1] & s->maxdata as the low and high bytes to the counter's reload registers, enables the timer and writes the GCB command to the counter command/status register. INSN_CONFIG_DISARM disables the timer. INSN_CONFIG_GET_COUNTER_STATUS reads the command/status register, sets data[1] to the COMEDI_COUNTER_COUNTING, _ARMED and _TERMINAL_COUNT bits for CIP, GCB and IP, acknowledges the interrupt when IP is set, and sets data[2] to the mask of those three bits. INSN_CONFIG_SET_COUNTER_MODE returns -EINVAL for a data[1] that is not I8254_MODE0 to MODE5 without any register access; otherwise it disables the timer and writes the Z8536 mode value for that 8254 mode. INSN_CONFIG_SET_CLOCK_SRC returns -EINVAL if data[1] > 2, otherwise stores data[1] (2 becomes 3) in devpriv->clk_src and writes it to the clock-select register. INSN_CONFIG_GET_CLOCK_SRC returns -EINVAL if devpriv->clk_src is not 0, 1 or 3, otherwise sets data[1] to 0, 1 or 2 and data[2] to the clock period in ns. INSN_CONFIG_SET_GATE_SRC returns -EINVAL if chan is 0; otherwise it reads the counter mode register, keeps only its EGE bit, sets EGE if data[1] == 1, returns -EINVAL (before writing) if data[1] > 1, and writes the result back, so data[1] == 0 keeps the existing EGE value and clears the other mode bits. INSN_CONFIG_GET_GATE_SRC returns -EINVAL if chan is 0 and otherwise does nothing. Any other data[0] returns -EINVAL. Every non-error path returns insn->n.
note: checked addi_apci_1500.c:586-715. Both reviewer claims RIGHT: GET_GATE_SRC only checks chan (706-709) and SET_GATE_SRC with data[1]==0 preserves EGE and clears the rest (698-704); old prose also wrongly said SET_GATE_SRC 'clears or sets' EGE.

name: pci9111_ai_do_cmd_test
prose: Precondition: dev, s and cmd are the comedi device, its analog-input subdevice and the command to check (cmd->chanlist may be NULL). Behaviour: it validates the command in five steps and returns at the first failing step: 1 if a trigger source is not one of the allowed values for start (TRIG_NOW), scan_begin (TRIG_TIMER, TRIG_FOLLOW or TRIG_EXT), convert (TRIG_TIMER or TRIG_EXT), scan_end (TRIG_COUNT) or stop (TRIG_COUNT or TRIG_NONE); 2 if scan_begin, convert or stop source is not a single source or if scan_begin_src is not TRIG_FOLLOW and differs from convert_src; 3 if an argument fails the range checks (start_arg 0, convert_arg and scan_begin_arg at least PCI9111_AI_ACQUISITION_PERIOD_MIN_NS for timer sources and 0 otherwise, scan_end_arg equal to chanlist_len, stop_arg at least 1 for TRIG_COUNT or 0 for TRIG_NONE); 4 if the timer-based convert_arg or scan_begin_arg changes when rounded to what the hardware can do; 5 if cmd->chanlist is non-NULL, chanlist_len > 0 and pci9111_ai_check_chanlist reports an error. It returns 0 if all steps pass. The comedi_check_trigger_* helpers it uses rewrite the offending cmd field with the accepted or rounded value, so cmd fields may be modified, including by steps that run before a later step returns a nonzero code.
note: slice cut head; real name is pci9111_ai_do_cmd_test (adl_pci9111.c:235-333). Checked each step against the code.

name: pci9118_ai_cmd
prose: Precondition: the command in s->async->cmd has passed the driver's cmdtest and dev->private, dev->pacer and s->async are valid. Behaviour: it records the command flags and start/stop conditions in devpriv (ai12_startstop, ai_neverending), decides usedma and the number of padding samples (ai_add_front, ai_add_back) from the bus-master flag, flags and convert source, and may raise cmd->convert_arg to ai_ns_min when a software sample-and-hold delay is needed. It computes the padded scan length; if that exceeds s->len_chanlist it logs an error and returns -EINVAL before touching the hardware. It then calls pci9118_set_chanlist, which programs the hardware chanlist. It then selects the acquisition mode ai_do: 1 or 4 when convert_src is TRIG_TIMER and scan_begin_src is not TRIG_TIMER (cascaded 8254 timers programmed, and in mode 4 the pacer is loaded and AM written to the config register); 2 when scan_begin_src is TRIG_TIMER and convert_src is not TRIG_EXT, which first returns -EIO (after the chanlist was already programmed) if usedma is 0; 3 when scan_begin_src is TRIG_FOLLOW and convert_src is TRIG_EXT. If ai_do is still 0 it logs an error and returns -EINVAL, also after the chanlist was programmed. Otherwise it sets the DMA bit in ai_ctrl if usedma, resets the config register to the default (burst and triggers disabled), resets the FIFO, clears status registers, sets up DMA (or enables the AMCC interrupt), starts the acquisition immediately if start_src is TRIG_NOW or installs pci9118_ai_inttrig as async->inttrig if it is TRIG_INT, enables the external trigger if start_src or stop_src is TRIG_EXT, and returns 0.
note: slice cut head; function is adl_pci9118.c:916-1139. Reviewer round 15 claim RIGHT: both -EIO (1065-1069) and -EINVAL (1098-1102) occur after pci9118_set_chanlist (1027); only the too-long -EINVAL (1017-1021) happens before any hardware access.

name: pci1760_pwm_insn_config
prose: Precondition: data[0] holds the INSN_CONFIG_* operation for the PWM channel chan = CR_CHAN(insn->chanspec), and data has the entries the operation uses. Behaviour: INSN_CONFIG_ARM first disables the channel through pci1760_pwm_enable (returning its negative error, which comes from pci1760_cmd, on failure), then returns -EINVAL if data[1] > 0xffff (the channel is already disabled at that point), otherwise sets the PWM count to data[1] and re-enables the channel, returning the first negative error from those commands. INSN_CONFIG_DISARM disables the channel. INSN_CONFIG_PWM_OUTPUT first disables the channel, then converts the high and low periods with pci1760_pwm_ns_to_div (data[1]/data[2] and data[3]/data[4] are rounding flag and period in ns) and returns -EINVAL if either rounding flag is not CMDF_ROUND_NEAREST, _UP or _DOWN; the divisor is clamped to 1..0xffff, and if a divisor times 100000 ns differs from the requested period for either value it overwrites data[2] and data[4] with the achieved periods and returns -EAGAIN without programming; otherwise it writes the high and low divisors and returns the first negative error from those commands; the channel is left disabled. INSN_CONFIG_GET_PWM_OUTPUT reads the high and low divisors from the device status, returns -ETIMEDOUT if either read fails, and otherwise stores the periods in ns in data[1] (high) and data[2] (low). INSN_CONFIG_GET_PWM_STATUS reads the enable mask, returning the negative error on failure, and stores 1 or 0 in data[1] for the channel. Any other data[0] returns -EINVAL with no device access. Successful operations return insn->n.
note: checked adv_pci1760.c:219-296, 176-217. Reviewer claims: round 1 RIGHT (ARM -EINVAL after disable), round 2 RIGHT (unsupported data[0] doesn't disable; divisors clamped), round 15 WRONG for GET_PWM_OUTPUT (it does store data[1],data[2], lines 280-281) and the -EAGAIN return exists in this function at line 263 (only the helper pci1760_pwm_ns_to_div never returns it).

name: me4000_ai_do_cmd_test
prose: Precondition: dev->private is a valid me4000_private, cmd is the command to test, and cmd->chanlist may be NULL. Behaviour: it runs five validation steps and returns at the first one that fails: 1 if a trigger source is not in the allowed set (start TRIG_NOW or TRIG_EXT, scan_begin TRIG_FOLLOW, TRIG_TIMER or TRIG_EXT, convert TRIG_TIMER or TRIG_EXT, scan_end TRIG_NONE or TRIG_COUNT, stop TRIG_NONE or TRIG_COUNT) - the comedi_check_trigger_src helper overwrites each source field with its value masked by the allowed set, so these source fields can be modified here; 2 if a source is not unique or the start/scan_begin/convert combination is not one of the six supported ones, where devpriv->ai_ctrl_mode is assigned (MODE_0, MODE_1, MODE_2 or MODE_0|MODE_1) for the matching combination only; 3 if the argument checks fail (start_arg must be 0; chanlist_len below 1 is set to 1; it then calls me4000_ai_round_cmd_args, which recomputes devpriv->ai_init_ticks, ai_scan_ticks and ai_chan_ticks, and replaces start_arg, scan_begin_arg or convert_arg with 2000, 2031 or 2000 when the tick count is too small; stop_arg must be at least 1 for TRIG_COUNT or 0 for TRIG_NONE); 4 if the combination-specific timing conflicts are found (start, convert or scan ticks below the minimum, scan time not longer than chanlist_len times the convert time, or scan_end_arg 0 with TRIG_COUNT), in which case it rewrites start_arg, convert_arg or scan_end_arg to corrected values and prints error messages; 5 if cmd->chanlist is non-NULL, chanlist_len > 0 and me4000_ai_check_chanlist reports an error. It returns 0 if all steps pass. cmd->flags is not modified.
note: checked me4000.c:711-925 and comedi_check_trigger_src (include/linux/comedi/comedidev.h:852-860). Reviewer claims: round 15 RIGHT (ai_ctrl_mode/ticks not set on step-1/2 early returns, nor in the else branch), round 2 half RIGHT (flags never modified) but WRONG that sources are never modified: comedi_check_trigger_src masks *src (line 858). Original round-1 claim about return 4 is WRONG: chanlist failure is return 5 (918-922).

name: daq700_dio_insn_bits
prose: Precondition: data[0] is the channel mask and data[1] the new bit values; data has at least two entries. Behaviour: it calls comedi_dio_update_state(s, data), which restricts data[0] to the subdevice's existing channels, updates s->state for those mask bits from data[1] and returns the restricted mask (it does not consult s->io_bits). If that mask is nonzero and any of its low 8 bits is set it writes s->state & 0xff to the DIO_W port. It then sets data[1] to (s->state & 0xff) | (inb(DIO_R) << 8), always reading DIO_R, and returns insn->n.
note: checked ni_daq_700.c:73-93 and comedi_dio_update_state (drivers.c:389-403). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the helper masks with the channel count, not io_bits; round 2 RIGHT: write needs a bit in the low 8 bits of the returned mask; round 1 RIGHT: value comes from data[1].

name: ni_E_init
prose: Precondition: dev->board_ptr, dev->private and dev->mmio are set up by the attach code, and interrupt_pin and irq_polarity are the board's interrupt pin selection and polarity flag. Behaviour: it returns -ENXIO if the build's IS_PCIMIO setting does not match whether dev->mmio is set, and -EINVAL if board->n_aochan > MAX_N_AO_CHAN. It looks up the signal routing tables (a missing table only prints warnings; if found it installs ni_global_insn_config and _ni_get_valid_routes), writes the clock-and-fout register, and calls comedi_alloc_subdevices, returning its error if it fails. It then fills in the analog input and output, digital I/O, 8255 (subdev_8255_cb_init, returning its error), calibration, EEPROM, PFI, cs5529, serial, RTSI, general-purpose counter and frequency-output subdevices, performing register writes along the way, and the analog output readback allocation (comedi_alloc_subdev_readback) whose error is returned. If ni_gpct_device_construct returns NULL it returns -ENOMEM. After the counters it programs the interrupt control register when dev->irq is set, writes the DMA select registers and some 6xxx or M-series registers, and returns 0. Returns from the middle of the function leave the earlier subdevices and register writes in place and undo nothing.
note: slice cut head; real function is ni_E_init (ni_mio_common.c:5985-6350), checked all returns: -ENXIO, -EINVAL, comedi_alloc_subdevices error, comedi_alloc_subdev_readback error, subdev_8255_cb_init error, -ENOMEM, 0. Old prose missed -ENXIO, -EINVAL and the alloc errors.

name: pcl724_8255mapped_io
prose: Precondition: iobase encodes the I/O base in its low 12 bits and a window index in bits 12 and up; dev is unused. Behaviour: it computes movport = I8255_SIZE * (iobase >> 12), masks iobase to its low 12 bits (iobase & 0x0fff), writes the byte port + movport to that I/O address (outb), and then, if dir is nonzero, writes the byte data to iobase + 1 and returns 0; if dir is zero it returns the byte read from iobase + 1 (inb, 0 to 255).
note: checked pcl724.c:78-92. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: iobase is masked at line 84 before the first outb at line 86, so the write goes to the masked address; the other round claims are consistent with the code.

name: rz_mtu3_action_read
prose: Precondition: counter, count, synapse and action are valid and belong together. Behaviour: it calls rz_mtu3_lock_if_count_is_enabled, which takes priv->lock and returns -EINVAL (releasing the lock) if the channel is busy and the count is not enabled; that error is returned with the lock not held. Otherwise it reads the count function from the TMDR1 phase-count mode via rz_mtu3_count_function_read_helper (which returns -EINVAL for an unsupported mode); on that error it releases the lock and returns it. It sets *action to COUNTER_SYNAPSE_ACTION_NONE. For counts other than MTU1 it reads TMDR3 and, when the PHCKSEL bit is set and the synapse signal is A or B, or the bit is clear and the signal is not A or B, it releases the lock and returns 0 leaving NONE. Otherwise it sets *action by function: PULSE_DIRECTION gives RISING_EDGE for signals A or C and NONE otherwise, QUADRATURE_X2_B gives BOTH_EDGES for signals B or D and NONE otherwise, QUADRATURE_X4 gives BOTH_EDGES, and any other function releases the lock and returns -EINVAL. It then releases the lock and returns 0. The lock is not held on any return.
note: checked rz-mtu3-cnt.c:628-698, 143-155, 201-229. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (NONE returned when PHCKSEL and signal pair mismatch, lines 658-662); round 2 RIGHT (lock helper checks is_busy && !count_is_enabled).

name: TRACE_EVENT(amd_pstate_perf,
prose: Generated function trace_amd_pstate_perf(min_perf, target_perf, capacity, freq, mperf, aperf, tsc, cpu_id, fast_switch), a static inline wrapper produced by TRACE_EVENT. It returns nothing; it takes the arguments by value and, when the amd_pstate_perf tracepoint is enabled, calls the registered probe functions with them; when the tracepoint is disabled it does nothing. The trace record is built by the probe callbacks defined from the event's TP_fast_assign, not by this wrapper.
note: TRACE_EVENT(amd_pstate_perf, ...) at amd-pstate-trace.h:25; TP_PROTO there is (u8 min_perf, u8 target_perf, u8 capacity, u64 freq, u64 mperf, u64 aperf, u64 tsc, unsigned int cpu_id, bool fast_switch). Old prose said the wrapper fills the event record; changed since the generated wrapper only dispatches to probes.

name: TRACE_EVENT(amd_pstate_epp_perf,
prose: Generated function trace_amd_pstate_epp_perf(cpu_id, highest_perf, epp, min_perf, max_perf, boost, changed), a static inline wrapper produced by TRACE_EVENT. It returns nothing; it takes the arguments by value and, when the amd_pstate_epp_perf tracepoint is enabled, calls the registered probe functions with them; when disabled it does nothing. The trace record is built by the probe callbacks defined from the event's TP_fast_assign, not by this wrapper.
note: TRACE_EVENT(amd_pstate_epp_perf, ...) at amd-pstate-trace.h:86; TP_PROTO (unsigned int cpu_id, u8 highest_perf, u8 epp, u8 min_perf, u8 max_perf, bool boost, bool changed).

name: cpufreq_policy_online
prose: Precondition: policy is an allocated cpufreq_policy, cpu is the CPU being onlined, new_policy says whether the policy was just created; the function takes the policy write lock itself (guard(cpufreq_policy_write)) and releases it on return. Behaviour: it sets policy->cpu and clears policy->governor. If the policy is not new and the driver has ->online it restores policy->cpus from related_cpus and calls ->online (failure goes to out_exit_policy); otherwise it sets policy->cpus to the one CPU, calls ->init (failure goes to out_clear_policy), runs cpufreq_table_validate_and_sort (failure goes to out_offline_policy) and copies cpus into related_cpus. It then intersects policy->cpus with cpu_online_mask. For a new policy it stores the policy in the per-CPU cpufreq_cpu_data of each related CPU, adds the CPU device symlinks, kzallocs the two QoS requests (-ENOMEM on failure) and adds the MIN and MAX requests, then notifies CPUFREQ_CREATE_POLICY; for an existing policy it updates the MAX request to policy->max. A failure of any of those QoS steps goes to out_destroy_policy. If the driver has ->get and a target it reads policy->cur and fails with -EIO if it is 0; if CPUFREQ_NEED_INITIAL_FREQ_CHECK is set and the current frequency is not in the table it retargets with __cpufreq_driver_target and BUG_ON a nonzero result. For a new policy only it then calls cpufreq_add_dev_interface, creates the stats table, adds the policy to cpufreq_policy_list and calls register_em if present. For both new and existing policies it then calls cpufreq_init_policy and returns 0 on success. Failures go to the unwind labels: out_destroy_policy removes the CPU device symlinks for policy->real_cpus and falls through to out_offline_policy (calls ->offline if present), then out_exit_policy (calls ->exit if present), then out_clear_policy (clears policy->cpus), and returns the error; the earlier labels start part-way through that chain. The QoS requests, related_cpus and the per-CPU cpufreq_cpu_data entries are not cleaned up by this function.
note: checked cpufreq.c:1383-1585. Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG for this tree: cpufreq_init_policy is called outside the new_policy block (lines 1560-1565), so for both new and existing policies; rounds 1-2 claims RIGHT (lock via guard, error path leaves QoS/related_cpus/per-cpu data). The old prose also wrongly said ->online is called for every existing policy; it needs cpufreq_driver->online.

name: cpufreq_core_init
prose: Precondition: called once at boot as a core initcall with no arguments. Behaviour: it reads the default governor via cpufreq_default_governor(), returns -ENODEV at once if cpufreq_disabled() is true, otherwise looks up the CPU subsystem's device root, creates the "cpufreq" kobject under it into cpufreq_global_kobject (and drops the device root reference) if the root exists, and then calls BUG_ON if cpufreq_global_kobject is still NULL. If the default_governor string is empty it copies the default governor's name into it with strscpy, then returns 0.
note: cpufreq.c:3031-3050. Contract left empty because it writes global state and the function returns an errno.
